title: Natural and transitive normalized open-refinement arrows
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For every scheme $T$ put $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, where $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ is the pulled-back ring and the category is the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Use the module direct images and inverse images of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], with the coefficient identifications induced by composition of pullbacks from the point and the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$, $j':U\hookrightarrow Z'$, $j'':U\hookrightarrow Z''$ be quasi-compact open immersions, and let $h:Z'\to Z$, $k:Z''\to Z'$ satisfy $hj'=j$, $kj''=j'$, $h^{-1}(j(U))=j'(U)$, and $k^{-1}(j'(U))=j''(U)$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the exact extension by zero of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] on ordinary unbounded derived categories. Let $\eta_j:1\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*j_!$ be its open adjunction unit, and let $r_h$ be [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction]. For every $K\in D_U$ define $e_{h,K}:j_!K\to Rh_*j'_!K$ to be the adjoint of $(r_h)^{-1}_{j'_!K}\eta_{j',K}$. It is the unique arrow satisfying
$$\eta_{j',K}^{-1}(r_h)_{j'_!K}j^*(e_{h,K})\eta_{j,K}=1_K.$$
These arrows are natural in $K$, $e_{1,K}=1_{j_!K}$ under the canonical identity constraints, and
$$\kappa_{h,k,j''_!K}\circ e_{hk,K}=Rh_*(e_{k,K})\circ e_{h,K},$$
where $\kappa$ is [lem-sfb-module-derived-compositor-coherence]. The assertions hold for all unbounded $K$; they do not assert invertibility of $e_{h,K}$. No properness or density is assumed.

proof.text: Use the actual ordinary unbounded open derived adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ specified in [def-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-comparisons]. The open unit is invertible by [lem-sfb-condensed-support-derived-localization], applied to $j$ and a closed immersion defining its complementary closed subset. Its hypotheses are a commutative condensed ring and a quasi-compact open immersion, both present here; it imposes no boundedness or constructibility. The same applies to $j'$ and $j''$. These are the coefficient-linear adjunctions and units of the statement, including their canonical alpha transport.

source.place: The restriction to X: exact open adjunction and invertible open unit

proof.text:
For $K,L\in D_U$ define
$$B_h(K,L):\operatorname{Hom}_{D_Z}(j_!K,Rh_*j'_!L)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D_U}(K,L),\quad a\longmapsto\eta_{j',L}^{-1}\circ(r_h)_{j'_!L}\circ j^*(a)\circ\eta_{j,K}.$$
This is a bijection: the specified open adjunction sends $a$ to $j^*(a)\circ\eta_{j,K}$, and postcomposition with the isomorphism $\eta_{j',L}^{-1}(r_h)_{j'_!L}$ is a bijection by [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction]. Explicitly its inverse sends $v:K\to L$ to $\varepsilon_{j,Rh_*j'_!L}\circ j_!((r_h)_{j'_!L}^{-1}\circ\eta_{j',L}\circ v)$; the two inverse identities are the two adjunction triangle identities followed by cancellation of these isomorphisms.

Set $e_{h,K}=B_h(K,K)^{-1}(1_K)$. Unwinding the preceding formula, its adjoint is precisely $(r_h)_{j'_!K}^{-1}\circ\eta_{j',K}$. Thus it is the arrow defined in the statement. The equality $B_h(K,K)(e_{h,K})=1_K$ is exactly the displayed normalization, and injectivity of $B_h(K,K)$ proves uniqueness.

source.place: (1) Uniqueness: existence and uniqueness of the normalized arrow

proof.text:
For any $u:K\to L$ apply $B_h(K,L)$ to the two arrows $Rh_*(j'_!u)\circ e_{h,K}$ and $e_{h,L}\circ j_!u$. Naturality of $r_h$ from [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction] and of $\eta_{j'}$ gives for the first image
$$\eta_{j',L}^{-1}\circ j'^*(j'_!u)\circ(r_h)_{j'_!K}\circ j^*(e_{h,K})\circ\eta_{j,K}=u.$$
Naturality of $\eta_j$ gives for the second image $B_h(L,L)(e_{h,L})\circ u=u$. Injectivity of $B_h(K,L)$ therefore gives $Rh_*(j'_!u)\circ e_{h,K}=e_{h,L}\circ j_!u$, the required naturality.

source.place: (1) Uniqueness, applied to a morphism K to L; (2), natural transformation assertion

proof.text: For $h=1_Z$ and $j'=j$, [lem-sfb-module-derived-compositor-coherence] identifies $R(1_Z)_*$ with the identity, and [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction] says that $r_{1_Z}$ is the identity under that comparison. Consequently $B_{1_Z}(K,K)(1_{j_!K})=\eta_{j,K}^{-1}\circ\eta_{j,K}=1_K$. Uniqueness from step 3 proves $e_{1,K}=1_{j_!K}$ under precisely these canonical identity constraints.

Put $A=j''_!K$ and $\beta=Rh_*(e_{k,K})\circ e_{h,K}$. On arrows $a:j_!K\to Rh_*Rk_*A$ the map
$$T(a)=\eta_{j'',K}^{-1}\circ(r_k)_A\circ(r_h)_{Rk_*A}\circ j^*(a)\circ\eta_{j,K}$$
is injective: it is the open-adjunction bijection followed by postcomposition with three isomorphisms supplied by the open units and [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction]. Naturality of $r_h$ at the arrow $e_{k,K}:j'_!K\to Rk_*A$ yields
$$(r_h)_{Rk_*A}\circ j^*Rh_*(e_{k,K})=j'^*(e_{k,K})\circ(r_h)_{j'_!K}.$$
Substitution and the two normalization equations from step 3 give
$$T(\beta)=\eta_{j'',K}^{-1}\circ(r_k)_A\circ j'^*(e_{k,K})\circ\eta_{j',K}=1_K.$$
This computes the actual composite, without assuming either refinement arrow invertible.

source.place: (3) Identity and transitivity: restriction of the composite arrow

proof.text:
The composite satisfies $(hk)j''=j$ and $(hk)^{-1}(j(U))=k^{-1}(j'(U))=j''(U)$, so step 3 applies to $hk$. The composition law in [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction], with the compositor of [lem-sfb-module-derived-compositor-coherence], reads
$$(r_{hk})_A=(r_k)_A\circ(r_h)_{Rk_*A}\circ j^*(\kappa_{h,k,A}).$$
It follows that $T(\kappa_{h,k,A}\circ e_{hk,K})=\eta_{j'',K}^{-1}\circ(r_{hk})_A\circ j^*(e_{hk,K})\circ\eta_{j,K}=1_K$. Comparing with step 6 and using injectivity of $T$ proves $\kappa_{h,k,A}\circ e_{hk,K}=Rh_*(e_{k,K})\circ e_{h,K}$. All calculations took place on the ordinary unbounded categories; no properness, density or field hypothesis was used.
